correctness.rationale: For every \(d\ge2\), Nielsen's exact identity reduces average fidelity to target-relative entanglement fidelity. A unitary channel has a pure normalized Choi state with spectrum \(\{1,0,\ldots,0\}\), while its overlap with the identity-target Choi vector is \(|\operatorname{Tr}U|^2/d^2\). Hence \(F_{\mathrm{avg}}=(|\operatorname{Tr}U|^2+d)/(d(d+1))\); the identity and a traceless diagonal root-of-unity unitary have identical Choi spectra but fidelities \(1\) and \(1/(d+1)\). Substituting the same unitary spectra into the anchor's formula yields \(1/d\) under normalized Choi convention and \(1\) under unnormalized convention, proving the stated contradiction. No finite experiment is used as the proof.

value.rationale: The error is not a harmless normalization typo: under the unnormalized convention it labels every coherent unitary error as perfect, while the true average fidelity can be as low as \(1/(d+1)\); under the normalized convention it even mislabels the identity. The correction therefore protects the paper's stated process-tomography/teleportation-fidelity workflow from replacing target-relative performance by Choi purity. It is a natural structural counterexample valid in every dimension, while remaining narrowly scoped to the erroneous appendix formula.
